paper_title: Millimeter-wave WISP search with coherent Light-Shining-Through-a-Wall towards the STAX project
suggested_experiment_name: STAX (Sub-THz-AXion) / Millimeter-wave WISP search with coherent Light-Shining-Through-a-Wall
coupling_convention: Kinetic mixing chi (dimensionless), canonical dark photon coupling
notes: This is a proposal/feasibility study paper, NOT a measurement of new exclusion limits. The paper presents PROJECTED sensitivities for three future stages (A, B, C) of a millimeter-wave LSW dark photon search at ~30 GHz targeting the mass range 10^-4 to 10^-3 eV. Stage A (low-power, commercial amplifier) is projected to reach χ ~ 10^-8 around m_γ' ~ 10^-4 eV (Section 4.1, Eq. 16). Figure 6 shows projected exclusion limits compared to existing constraints (CROWS, UWA, Yale, darkSRF, ALPS, ALPSIIb). The paper explicitly states this is 'an essential step towards axion LSW in the millimeter-wave range (STAX experiment)' and represents proto-STAX development. No actual measured data or observed exclusion limits are presented—only theoretical projections and proof-of-concept demonstrations of coherent detection at 30 GHz. The coupling type is unambiguously DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing χ with ordinary photons in LSW geometry). Extraction confidence is moderate (0.65) because while the coupling type is clear, the actual numerical projections in Figure 6 are not explicitly tabulated in the text; Stage A sensitivity χ ~ 10^-8 is derived from Eq. (16) with stated parameters.
